eventID: An identifier for the set of information associated with a dwc:Event (something that occurs at a place and time). May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.
occurrenceID: An identifier for the dwc:Occurrence (as opposed to a particular digital record of the dwc:Occurrence). In the absence of a persistent global unique identifier, construct one from a combination of identifiers in the record that will most closely make the dwc:occurrenceID globally unique.
measurementType: The nature of the measurement, fact, characteristic, or assertion. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. See also http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/index.htm#measurementType
measurementValue: The value of the measurement, fact, characteristic, or assertion. See also http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/index.htm#measurementValue
measurementUnit: The units associated with the measurementValue. Recommended best practice is to use the International System of Units (SI). See also http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/index.htm#measurementUnit
measurementMethod: A description of or reference to (publication, URI) the method or protocol used to determine the measurement, fact, characteristic, or assertion. See also http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/index.htm#measurementMethod
measurementRemarks: Comments or notes accompanying the MeasurementOrFact. See also http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/index.htm#measurementRemarks

eventID: eventID will remain blank if the emof information is not associated with a specific event
occurrenceID: occurrenceID will remain blank if the emof information is not associated with a specific occurrence
measurementValue: measurementValue and measurementUnit are paired terms and should be populated together.

measurementRemarks: r - Rare, with very few individuals and negligible cover: + - Few individuals, with a small cover (can be up to 5% of the plot: 1 - Numerous individuals, but with a low cover (less than 5% of the plot): 2 - Very abundant, covering less than 5% of the plot: 2a - Covering between 5% and 12.5% of the plot: 2b - Covering between 12.5% and 25% of the plot: 3 - Covering between 25% and 50% of the plot: 4 - Covering between 50% and 75% of the plot: 5 - Covering between 75% and 100% of the plot
